land.text: Okinawa Island, where 'the last overlord of Tenson dynasty was assassinated' by Riyū, whom Shunten overthrew

predecessors.note: The legendary Tenson line of the Chūzan Seikan; Cliopatria has no row and no dossier is planned, so the land is nobody's before 1187.

land.text: central Okinawa around Urasoe, where the Eiso kings Tamagusuku and Seii continued as Chūzan to 1349

successors.note: Cliopatria's 'Chüzan' row (1314-1428) carries the Eiso line's last two kings.

land.text: the north: the lord of Nakijin 'declared himself independent of Chūzan and crowned himself as the King of Hokuzan'
the south: 'The lord (aji) of Ōzato left for his own castle and declared himself to be King of Nanzan'

capitals.name: Urasoe
capitals.note: Shunten 'was the lord of Urasoe' before becoming king and Satto was 'the Governor of Urasoe' when he seized the throne in 1350 (Eiso page); neither page names a capital, so Urasoe is the researcher's reading.

rulers.title: king (paramount chief)

correction.text: unchanged: Okinawa Island as Cliopatria draws it, from 1187 ('In 1187, Shunten was recognized as the new king')

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria begins in 1188. 2,186 km2 against Okinawa Island's roughly 1,200 km2: the shape takes in nearby islands or a generous coastline. The page gives no extent and calls the kings 'paramount chiefs, or overlords among aji during the Gusuku period', so the whole-island shape is Cliopatria's reading; unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged; holds 1305 to 1314, when the island 'split into three principalities: Chūzan, Nanzan and Hokuzan'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria ends the row in 1313 and starts Chüzan, Hokuzan and Nanzan in 1314, the page's split year (one-year overlap convention). The 1305 break (identical area) is unexplained; Taisei died in 1308 and Eiji succeeded in 1309.

region.text: Okinawa Island, in 'the traditional historiography of Okinawa Island'

ledger.note: 1187: Shunten, lord of Urasoe, recognised as king of Okinawa. 'In 1187, Shunten was recognized as the new "king", overlord among aji' after he 'revolted against Riyū and overthrew him'; legend makes 'his father, Minamoto no Tametomo, ... an adventurer from Japan'. The rulers 'should be more accurately identified as paramount chiefs'.

1259: Gihon abdicates to his regent Eiso; the Eiso dynasty. 'It was established by Eiso in 1259'; 'Around 1254, Gihon appointed Eiso to be regent' and 'Seven years later, Gihon abdicated in favor of Eiso'; the king table gives Eiso 1260–1299 and the Shunten page ends Gihon's reign in 1259. Same realm, same colour (rule 2).

1314: Hokuzan breaks away. 'When the fourth ruler Tamagusuku ascended the throne in 1314' the island 'split into three principalities: Chūzan, Nanzan and Hokuzan'; the lord of Nakijin 'declared himself independent of Chūzan and crowned himself as the King of Hokuzan'.
1314: Nanzan breaks away. 'The lord (aji) of Ōzato left for his own castle and declared himself to be King of Nanzan.'

region.text: Okinawa Island, divided between Chūzan, Hokuzan and Nanzan

ledger.note: 1314: the Sanzan period; the Eiso kings continue as Chūzan at Urasoe. The line ruled Chūzan until 'the death of the last king Seii in 1349', when 'Satto, the Governor of Urasoe, seized the throne for himself and established the Satto dynasty' (1350); Cliopatria's Chüzan row begins in 1314.

wars.name: Shunten's revolt against Riyū
wars.outcome: 'Shunten revolted against Riyū and overthrew him'; 'In 1187, Shunten was recognized as the new king'.

certainty.note: A Gusuku-period chiefdom: no borders on the pages; the extent beyond Urasoe (the whole island, the Kerama and Kume islands, Amami) is unverified.

sources.title: Shunten dynasty
sources.note: Identity, 1187-1259, the three kings, Urasoe, Riyū, Tametomo legend; no area.

sources.title: Eiso dynasty
sources.note: 1259/1260-1349, the five kings, the 1314 split, Satto 1350; no tribute records, no area.

notes: One dossier for the Shunten (1187-1259) and Eiso (1259-1349) lines, a dynasty change on the same island (rule 2); it ends in 1314 because Cliopatria's Chüzan row (1314-1428, written by another jk-01 part) carries the last Eiso kings Tamagusuku and Seii after the Sanzan split, so the chuzan dossier should begin with a predecessor link to shunten-dynasty and the 1349-1350 Satto change as a rename. Cliopatria 1188-1313 against the pages' 1187-1314. The Eiso accession is dated 1259 (dynasty), 1260 (king table) or about 1261 ('Seven years later' than c. 1254) by the Eiso page. Not on the pages opened: the tribute of Kumejima, Kerama and Iheya (1264) and Amami Ōshima (1266), the Tomari office, the Yuan contacts of 1291 and 1296, any area; the extent of the paramountcy beyond Urasoe is Cliopatria's whole-island reading. Capital Urasoe is a reading of both pages. The Tenson predecessor is legendary and has no row.
